title: C528/720/2024 of RAHUL MAURYA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
2024:UHC:7942
1
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc Application No. 720 of 2024
23 October, 2024

Rahul Maurya --Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand & Others --Respondents
Presence:-
Mr. Sandeep Tiwari, counsel for the petitioner/accused.
Mr. G. S. Sandhu, learned Additional Advocate General assisted by
Ms. Mamta Joshi, learned Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Piyush Tiwari, counsel for the respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Hon'ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.
This criminal misc. application is filed under
Section 528 of B.N.S.S. by the petitioner/accused for
quashing the entire proceedings pending in the court
of Additional District & Sessions Judge/Fast Track
Court/Special Judge (POCSO), Haldwani in Special
Session Trial No. 73 of 2022 'State vs. Rahul Maurya'
for the offence punishable under Section 376(3) of
IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
2. Counsel for the petitioner/accused would
submit that an F.I.R. was lodged by the respondent
no.3/complainant (father of respondent no.2/victim)
against the present petitioner alleging therein that
the present petitioner had made physical relationship
with his daughter by which she got pregnant; that,
the Investigating Officer after completion of
investigation submitted charge-sheet against the
petitioner/accused under Section 376(3) I.P.C. and
5/6 of POCSO Act.

2024:UHC:7942
2
3. He would further submit that during the
trial, on 28.01.2023 the respondent no.2/victim has
been examined as PW1, she stated that the age of the
prosecutrix/victim is 19 years, therefore, at the time
of the alleged incident i.e. 27.07.2022, the
prosecutrix/victim was more than 18 years of age;
that, now the marriage between the
petitioner/accused and respondent no.2/victim was
solemnized on 07.03.2024 and both are continuously
discharging their matrimonial obligations.
4. Counsel for the petitioner/accused would
further submit that the parties have settled the
dispute amicably and the respondents do not want to
prosecute the petitioner/accused further, therefore, a
joint Compounding Application (IA No. 01 of 2024)
has been filed by the parties to compound the alleged
offence and prayed that the entire proceedings of the
criminal case be quashed.
5. Per contra, learned State counsel
vehemently opposed the compounding application on
the ground that the offences alleged against the
petitioner/accused are non-compoundable and the
same cannot be compounded even with the
permission of the Court under Section 359 of
B.N.S.S. even if the compromise have taken place
between the petitioner/accused and the respondent
no.2 & 3; that, in such type of serious offence, the
criminal proceedings cannot be quashed though, the
victim and the offender have settled the dispute
amicably, as such offences are not private but have a
serious impact upon the Society.

2024:UHC:7942
3
6. Learned State counsel would further submit
that in the charge-sheet, school records of the
prosecutrix/victim were also filed, in accordance with
which, the respondent no.2/victim was 14 years of
age at time of the alleged incident; that, the trial of
the case is on final stage as now the case is fixed
before the trial court for the statement of the
petitioner/accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. and
the statements of the other witnesses have also not
been annexed with this petition; that, the offence
alleged against the petitioner/accused is heinous,
therefore, there is no ground for quashing the
criminal proceedings at this stage.
7. It is trite that the powers under Section 528
of B.N.S.S. have to be exercised sparingly, carefully
and with caution and only to prevent abuse of
process of any Court or otherwise to secure ends of
justice.
8. In the considered view of this Court, this is
not a fit case in which, the powers under Section 528
of B.N.S.S. should be exercised.
9. Accordingly, the present C-528 petition
lacks merit and the same is hereby dismissed in
limine.
10. Let a copy of this order be sent to the court
concerned for necessary compliance.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.)
 23.10.2024
